matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked by 7.9 points this week—close enough to taste victory, far enough away that he'll be thinking about it for three goddamn days. Rinor's team showed up with a pulse while Rob's lineup decided to collectively phone it in like they were getting paid to underperform. That's what happens when you build a roster held together with duct tape and false hope—one mediocre week from Rinor is enough to expose you as the fraud you've been running all season.

Adam came in this week looking like he had a fucking plan, and that plan was apparently to field a roster of ghosts and broken promises. Down 11.2 points, this isn't even a loss—it's a mercy killing. Flamur rolled out competent lineups like a functional adult while Adam's team went full dumpster fire, proving once again that his draft strategy of "hope and prayer" doesn't cut it in actual competition.

Rilind got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 62 goddamn points—that's not a matchup, that's a war crime. Whatever shit roster decisions you made this season finally caught up with you in the most brutal way possible, and frankly, you should be embarrassed to show your face at draft day next year. Arben didn't even need to field a competent team; your incompetence did half the work for him. Maybe spend less time fucking around and more time actually paying attention to who's injured before Sunday.

Jetmir and Peter got absolutely skullfucked this week, losing by 57.7 points like they showed up to the draft drunk and forgot what positions actually do. Between the two of you, you managed to field a roster that looked like a practice squad reject pile, and it shows—143 to 85 is the kind of beat-down that makes you question whether either of you have ever actually watched football. Nori didn't just win, he buried you so deep in the dirt that archaeologists are gonna find your team's remains in 2087 wondering what the fuck went wrong.

Ben got absolutely skullfucked by 8.8 points this week, and honestly, it's hard to tell if his team choked or if he just drafted like someone who's never watched football before. 98.4 points is nothing to write home about, but Ben managed to score even less while having a full roster—that takes a special kind of incompetence. He's down by nearly 9 and probably still trying to figure out why his studs looked like practice squad players come Sunday.

Veton got absolutely dicked down 117.4 to 100.7 this week—a 16.7 point ass-whooping that would've been respectable if he wasn't facing a team that looked like it was set and forget through a fucking hurricane. Faton's out here playing checkers while Veton's still trying to figure out which end of the roster is which, and it fucking shows. That margin might as well be 50 points the way Veton's team shit the bed, and now he gets to spend the rest of the week wondering where it all went wrong—spoiler alert: everywhere.

matchups.preview: Rob's sitting at 0-3 like he's actively trying to tank for draft picks, and now he's got to face Flamur who's actually figured out how to field a competent roster—which shouldn't be hard when you're playing against the guy who thought reaching for a backup tight end in round 4 was "value." Flamur's about to add another W to the highlight reel while Rob's still out here wondering why his "championship team" can't win a single goddamn game.

Arben's sitting pretty at 3-0 but let's be real—that's just the luck window before the regression freight train hits. Rinor's only two games back and already sniffing blood, because Arben's got the consistency of a coin flip and we all know which way this thing's about to land. This is the week the undefeated gets exposed, and Rinor's going to be the one holding the hammer.

Nori's sitting pretty at 2-1 thinking he's figured this out, but we all know that's just the league's way of lulling him into a false sense of security before he catastrophically implodes—meanwhile Adam's desperate ass at 1-2 is going to come out swinging like he's got nothing to lose, which, spoiler alert, he doesn't. This is the matchup where one guy realizes his "genius" was just dumb luck and the other remembers why he's been ass all season long.

Ben's sitting at 1-2 with a roster that screams "panic drafted after three beers," while Rilind's right there in the mud with him—except Rilind at least has the excuse of actually showing up to the waiver wire. This is a matchup between two guys desperately trying to convince themselves they're not completely fucked, and spoiler alert: one of you is about to lose to the other disaster and feel even worse about it.

Veton's already digging himself out of a 0-3 grave while Jetmir/Peter roll in at 1-2 thinking they're hot shit because they lucked into one win—but this week, Veton gets to prove that rock bottom was just a pit stop on the way to taking a team that actually has a pulse to the woodshed. Even a blind squirrel finds a nut eventually, and Veton's desperation is about to turn into the kind of ass-beating that makes you question why you even drafted this roster.

Faton's sitting pretty at 2-1, but let's be honest—that record is held together with duct tape and prayer, carried entirely by whatever waiver-wire lottery ticket went off. Meanwhile Ilir's been equally mediocre, just with better luck so far. This week one of you frauds finally gets exposed, and my money's on whoever drafted more injured players hoping they'd magically heal mid-season. May the least incompetent manager win.
